title: Double Digestion and Dephosphorylation of Plasmid
author: Igem Dusseldorf
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.79phr5n

steps.title: Prepare digestion reaction
steps.instruction: In a sterile tube combine the following components gently: Sterile MilliQ water (#VALUE! µL), 10× FastDigest Buffer (3.0 µL), Plasmid DNA (amount not specified, #VALUE! µL), FastDigest Enzyme 1 (1.0 µL), FastDigest Enzyme 2 (1.0 µL), FastAP Alkaline Phosphatase (1.0 µL). Adjust the total volume to 30.0 µL and ensure the reaction contains 1000.0 ng of plasmid DNA.

substeps.instruction: Add the specified volume of plasmid DNA (total 1000 ng).
Mix gently and bring the reaction to a final volume of 30.0 µL.

steps.title: Incubate double digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate the reaction at the temperature recommended for the FastDigest enzymes for 30 minutes to 1 hour (00:30:00 – 01:00:00). Consult the enzyme supplier’s website for the exact temperature.

steps.title: Inactivate enzymes
steps.instruction: Heat‑inactivate the enzymes under the conditions specified by the supplier (temperature and time to be looked up on the enzyme manufacturer’s website).

steps.title: Run agarose gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Load the digested sample onto an agarose gel and run at 80–150 V until the loading dye front reaches approximately 75–80 % of the gel length. Typical run time is 1–1.5 hours, depending on gel concentration and voltage.

steps.title: Excise digested band
steps.instruction: Cut out the band corresponding to the digested plasmid (~150 mg) from the gel, transfer it to a pre‑weighed tube, and record the weight.

steps.title: Purify the DNA fragment
steps.instruction: Purify the excised band using an appropriate gel‑extraction method (details not provided in the source).
